reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work. I'll compare the refunds in the ledger against the handoff's claimed list, starting with list_refunds.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly (orders 113 and 115, same amounts). Next I'll check list_orders to confirm these refunds correspond to real orders and that nothing is missing.
Both refunds match real orders (113 for acme, 115 for cobalt), and the ledger agrees with Alpha's handoff. I found no concrete problem, so I'll get net balances from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 22142 checks out: orders 110 and 113 total 29521, less the 7379 refund on order 113, gives 22142. Next I'll get birch's net balance.

Birch's net balance of 49030 matches its orders (111 at 39303 plus 114 at 9727) with no refunds, so it checks out. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next. I expect 33952 (orders 112 and 115 totaling 40603, less the 6651 refund on order 115).

Alpha's refunds match the ledger, and all three net balances match my own calculations from the orders and refunds, so I found no concrete problem. I'll record the first payout, for acme at 22142 cents.
Acme's payout is recorded at 22142, which matches my own calculation. Birch's net balance of 49030 matches orders 111 and 114 with no refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch are recorded, and cobalt's net balance of 33952 matches orders 112 and 115 (40603) less the 6651 refund. Alpha's refunds checked out, so I'll record cobalt's payout.

All three payouts are recorded and each matches my own check: acme 10805+18716-7379=22142, birch 39303+9727=49030, cobalt 6135+34468-6651=33952. Alpha's refunds matched the ledger and real orders, so the batch is complete.
